about: Q-0080: what a backlog allocates, as one table both trees assert over — spike/test/q0080-allocation.js
and packages/core/src/backlog/backlog.test.ts. A fix in one tree alone passes its own suite and
leaves the other handing out T-0001; two transcriptions of a table drift the same way, so there
is one. Each row builds a backlog from `tickets` ([folder, id]) and asks nextId() for `id`, or
expects it to throw `throws` — the whole message, because a refusal that names no evidence is
the defect this ticket is about. It is a .json rather than a .js so spike/test/run.js, which
discovers *.js, does not try to execute it.

rows.name: an empty backlog starts where harness init says it does
the prefix comes from the ids on disk
an adopter's own prefix needs no configuration
the counter still works when the prefix matches
the maximum is numeric, not lexicographic
matching is exact and case-sensitive, so no near miss advances the counter
tickets are there and no id parses: refuse, with the count and a sample
rows.throws: cannot allocate a ticket id: read 3 tickets and none has an id of the form <PREFIX>-nnnn (saw 'Q-12', 'T-1', 'q-0011'); pass --id <ID> or reconcile the backlog

rows.name: the sample is bounded, so a large damaged backlog still prints one line
rows.throws: cannot allocate a ticket id: read 4 tickets and none has an id of the form <PREFIX>-nnnn (saw 'a-1', 'b-2', 'c-3', …); pass --id <ID> or reconcile the backlog

rows.name: more than one prefix parses: refuse, naming every prefix and its count
rows.throws: cannot allocate a ticket id: the backlog uses more than one prefix — Q- (2), T- (1); pass --id <ID> or reconcile the backlog

rows.name: the prefix is full: a five-digit id is not one harness runs could resolve
rows.throws: cannot allocate a ticket id: the next id after T-9999 would be T-10000, which is not of the form <PREFIX>-nnnn; pass --id <ID> or reconcile the backlog
